activity.heading: Activity requirements
activity.lead: To keep the community active and worthwhile, members are expected to:

attend.title: Attend at least 2 gatherings a year.
attend.body: Gatherings include in-person meetings, workshops and social events.

slack.title: Be active in the Slack channel.
slack.body: Join discussions, share experiences and ask questions.

absence.title: Let us know if you will be away.
absence.body: If you know you will be less active for a while, tell the board.

activity.review: The board reviews activity levels regularly. If the requirements are not met over time, the board may get in touch for a conversation about the way forward.

retirement.heading: Retirement
retirement.body: A member who does not meet the activity requirements over a longer period may be retired by the board. Retirement is not a punishment, but a recognition that life and priorities change.

meaning.slack: You keep access to Slack, but lose access to private channels and are moved to a retired role.
meaning.events: You cannot attend roundtable gatherings, but you are welcome at social events.
meaning.vote: You have no vote at the annual general meeting.
meaning.rejoin: You can ask the board at any time to become an active member again.

reinstatement.heading: Rejoining
reinstatement.body: Want to become an active member again? Get in touch with the board. We consider rejoining based on your intent and your capacity to take an active part.

host.title: Hosting
host.intro: Let us know you are interested in hosting. It is not a commitment: the board gets in touch when we plan the next gathering and matches you with a suitable topic and group. The gatherings themselves are booked through Luma.
host.formIntro: All fields are optional: signing up is signal enough. The board sets up the gathering in Luma when it is your turn.

form.capacity: How many people can you host?
form.timeframePlaceholder: e.g. Q3 2026, before the summer, flexible
form.error: Could not register. Please try again.

openToWork.title: Open to work
openToWork.intro: We are regularly asked whether we know someone for a CTO role. If you are in a new situation, or just curious about what is out there, you can mark yourself as open here. By default you are not listed. The list is only visible to members of the investment groups and the board, since that is where the requests come in. You can withdraw at any time.
openToWork.isOpen: You are listed as open to new opportunities
openToWork.notListed: You are not listed. All fields are optional, signing up is enough.

form.availabilityPlaceholder: e.g. now, from January, 3 months' notice

security.title: Sign-in
security.intro: You sign in with a link sent by email. With a passkey you can sign in with Face ID, your fingerprint or a security key instead, without waiting for the email. The email link keeps working, so if you lose your device, just sign in with the link and remove the passkey here.

add.heading: Add a passkey
add.headingOnboarding: One more step: set up a passkey for {name}
add.unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys. You can still sign in with the email link.
add.storage: The passkey is stored on this device (or in iCloud Keychain / Google Password Manager, so it follows you to your other devices). We only store the public key.
add.added: Passkey added. Next time you can choose "{button}" on the sign-in page.
add.signOutAndIn: Sign out and sign in again
add.reauthDone: Confirmed. Press "{button}" again to add the new passkey.

list.heading: Your passkeys

errors.loadList: Could not load your passkeys. Please try again.

errors.duplicate: This passkey has already been added.

errors.rename: Could not rename it. Please try again.
errors.remove: Could not remove the passkey. Please try again.
errors.reauth: For security reasons you can only add a passkey right after you have signed in. Confirm with a passkey you already have, or sign out and sign in again with the email link, and try again.
errors.limit: You already have {max} passkeys. Remove one you do not use, then you can add a new one.
errors.reauthFailed: Confirming with a passkey did not work. Try again, or sign out and sign in again.

device.title: Connect an agent
device.intro: An agent (for example the ctr CLI on a box) is asking for access to the portal's admin API. Check that you started it yourself and that the code matches the one in the terminal. Only then approve.
device.boardOnly: Only the board (styret) can connect agents.

scopes.eventsWrite: create events and record attendance from Luma
scopes.surveysWrite: create, close and send out surveys

device.tokenNote: Approving gives this agent a token in your name for {days} days, with exactly this access. It stops working if you leave the board, and everything it does is logged.
device.reauth: For security reasons you can only approve right after signing in. Confirm it is you with a passkey and you can approve straight away. No passkey? Sign out and sign in again with the email link, then open the link from the terminal again.
device.signOutAndIn: Sign out and sign in again
device.approved: Approved. The agent picks up its token within a few seconds, and you can close this page.
device.denied: Denied. The agent gets no access.

surveys.title: Surveys
surveys.intro: Short surveys after our events. They take a couple of minutes, and they are how we find out what worked and what we should do differently next time. The board sees the answers.

sweden.title: CTO Roundtable Sweden
sweden.intro: This is the Stockholm chapter's own space. The evenings and surveys here are for the Swedish chapter only.
sweden.noUpcoming: No evening is set up yet. It will show here and on Luma.
sweden.sharedBody: Offers from partner companies, and investor updates if you are part of an investment cohort.

how.a: An evening every one to two months. One company presents its setup, the host offers pizza and something to drink, and the rest is three hours of honest questions. 10 to 15 CTOs, invite-only.

who.a: CTOs (or the person doing that job), invited by an existing member.

norway.q: How is this related to the Norwegian network?
norway.a: Same model, separate group. Separate evenings, a separate channel, no shared invitations. Offers and the investment side are shared.

question.a: Ask in #roundtable-sweden, or reply to your invitation email.

list.title: Cases
list.intro: The companies the committee is reviewing for your SPV, and the votes on them. The raw material is here (deck, notes from the founder calls, numbers), with the memo next to it.
list.staffNote: You see this as committee or board: drafts and every SPV included.
list.empty: No cases to show right now.

case.materialIntro: Raw material first, the memo last. Read what you need.
case.materialNotShared: The committee has not shared material on this company yet. You can still ask and give input.
case.staffNote: You see this case as committee or board.

qa.title: Questions and answers
qa.intro: Ask what you want to know. An agent answers from the material above, usually within a few minutes, and says so when the answer is not there. Then the question goes to the owner of the case. The answer is shown to everyone in the SPV. Only the committee sees who asked.
qa.asked: Thanks! You get an email when it is answered.
qa.routedTo: Sent to {name}, who owns the case.
qa.routedToNote: Sent to {name}, who owns the case. The agent: «{note}»
qa.waiting: 1 question from others is waiting for an answer. | {count} questions from others are waiting for an answer.
qa.answerLabel: The answer (shown to everyone in the SPV)
qa.fromFounder: The answer comes from the founder

status.new: Waiting for an answer. You get an email when it comes.
status.newOther: Waiting for the agent to answer.
status.routed: The agent did not find the answer in the material. It went to the owner of the case.
status.founder_asked: Asked the founder. The answer will come here.

label.agent: Answer from an agent, not yet checked by the committee
label.agentConfirmed: Answer from an agent, confirmed by the committee
label.agentConfirmedBy: Answer from an agent, confirmed by {name}
label.founder: Answer from the founder, via the committee

comments.title: Input for the committee
comments.intro: Do you have objections, suggestions or questions for the founder, or do you know them? Write it here. The committee sees it with your name. The other members do not see it, so nobody is swayed by what others write. It does not count as a vote.
comments.introStaff: What the members have written, with names. Each member sees only their own. You can write here too.

placeholder.suggestion: What should the committee do or check?
placeholder.founder_question: What should the committee ask the founder?
placeholder.signal: How do you know them, and what do you know?

comments.sent: Sent. Only the committee sees it.

ballot.backfill: Vote by email, closed {date}. Only the counts were recorded.
ballot.draftNote: Draft. Members do not see the vote until it is opened.
ballot.openConfirm: Opening locks the list of who may vote in {group}, and the deadline becomes 48 hours from now. The job sends the email and Slack notices.
ballot.standingBlank: You stand as blank until you vote yourself.
ballot.conflict: You are marked as conflicted on this company and can only vote blank.
ballot.changeUntil: You can change your vote until the deadline. The last one counts.
ballot.notOnRoster: You are not on the voting list of {group}.
ballot.secret: You see the counts, not who voted what. The committee sees the names. The proposal passes with at least 2/3 yes of the yes and no votes.

committee.title: The committee's overview
committee.intro: Every case with what waits for the committee: questions sent to the owner of the case, agent answers not yet confirmed, and new input since the last summary.
committee.forbidden: For the committee and the board only.
committee.routed: 1 question waits for the owner | {count} questions wait for the owner
committee.unconfirmed: 1 agent answer to confirm | {count} agent answers to confirm
committee.withAgent: 1 question with the agent | {count} questions with the agent

pipeline.title: The pipeline
pipeline.intro: What the committee is working on now, up for a vote and in review first. Ask, raise an objection, or say you know them, long before a vote. The committee sees who wrote; the other members do not.
pipeline.introInvested: The companies your SPV invested in. The pipeline being worked on now is for the SPV that is investing now.
pipeline.workingEmpty: No companies to show right now.
pipeline.audience: Only the members of {groups} and the committee see this.
pipeline.showDeclined: Show the ones we said no to
pipeline.declinedIntro: Companies the committee reviewed and said no to.

conflict.title: Conflict of interest?
conflict.intro: Do you work at the company, own part of it, or have another tie to it? Then you can only vote blank when it comes to a vote (mandate §9). Say so here and it is recorded. Only the committee sees who has said so.
conflict.declared: You have declared a conflict ({date}). You can only vote blank on this company.
conflict.lockedWhileOpen: A vote is open now, so it cannot be withdrawn until the vote is over.
conflict.openRoundNote: The vote that is open now has already locked its list of voters. Vote blank there yourself. This applies from the next vote.
conflict.staffLabel: 1 has declared a conflict | {count} have declared a conflict

pipelineDigest.draftIntro: Made by {who}. It goes to everyone in the SPV by email and Slack once a committee member approves it. For the first four weeks the committee approves each one; after that it goes out on its own.
